name: SDI/PRT Feasibility Reframe
head: 7eea01fc9
corrected_objective: Can SDI/PRT make larger dense models run inside CPU/RAM limits where the native path fails, swaps, or becomes unusable?
core_framing: Any coherent generation is faster than impossible.
feasibility_success: Model loads or partially streams without OOM
Speed can be slow but not frozen
Memory behavior stable under strict guard
feasibility_non_success: Only works by pretending smaller model is larger model
why_speed_first_wrong: Already-runnable models aren't the target — if 7B runs fine, speed optimization has diminishing returns vs solving the harder problem
Speed on working hardware ≠ feasibility on impossible hardware — 10% speedup on 7B doesn't move needle on running 14B/30B in 16GB RAM

capacity_first_prt.question: Can model weights be represented or activated progressively so that a model larger than available comfortable RAM can still generate?
mechanisms: Progressive residual weight planes (load on demand, not all at once)
Native-layout compressed sidecars (structured compression, not raw f32)
Layer/block paging with strict memory budget (never materialize full model)
Partial activation of FFN/channel blocks (skip what's not needed)
Low-rank/residual reconstruction on demand (approximate weights cheaply)
Verification/fallback against native where possible (blend paths)
hard_constraints: Smaller resident footprint than naive full-weight load
Bounded working set — never exceeds available RAM + guard margin
No sidecar larger than what it replaces
Native/backend layout considered from day one

best_first_target: 14B on 16GB RAM — truly impossible for naive native path, not so large as to require radical compression, real-world relevance, lower risk than 30B

feasibility_benchmark.native_baseline: Attempt model load+generation under strict memory guard; record OOM/swap/failure/unusable speed; pass if native fails or unusable
feasibility_benchmark.sdi_prt_candidate: Same prompt/task; same strict guard; record coherent output check+memory delta+time; pass if produces coherent answer without swap death
feasibility_benchmark.pass_threshold: Native fails/unusable AND SDI/PRT produces coherent answer for all 3 task types without swap death

recommended_next_phase: Phase 28E: 14B feasibility analysis + capacity-first PRT requirements — analysis and design only, no running 14B yet
